title: A Creative Cutout
statementMd:
*Everything red frightens Nian the monster. So do red paper and... you, red on Codeforces, potential or real.*

Big Banban has got a piece of paper with endless lattice points, where lattice points form squares with the same area. His most favorite closed shape is the circle because of its beauty and simplicity. Once he had obtained this piece of paper, he prepares it for paper-cutting.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/82edc897487bb94b56952d372bcbcb46bd964bb6.png)

He drew $*n*$ concentric circles on it and numbered these circles from $1$ to $*n*$ such that the center of each circle is the same lattice point and the radius of the $*k*$-th circle is ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/bd3647accc3b41427aa4218c550a610cef4bfdeb.png) times the length of a lattice edge.

Define the degree of beauty of a lattice point as the summation of the **indices** of circles such that this lattice point is inside them, or on their bounds. Banban wanted to ask you the total degree of beauty of all the lattice points, but changed his mind.

Defining the total degree of beauty of all the lattice points on a piece of paper with $*n*$ circles as $*f*(*n*)$, you are asked to figure out ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/1c6463774e657bd7c8665c65ff8deb39afdcf644.png).

## Input

The first line contains one integer $*m*$ $(1 ≤ *m* ≤ 10^{12})$.

## Output

In the first line print one integer representing ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/1c6463774e657bd7c8665c65ff8deb39afdcf644.png).

## Note

A piece of paper with $5$ circles is shown in the following.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/b63097ed9dc567853f8c13b2a90317a6ad36bb91.png)

There are $5$ types of lattice points where the degree of beauty of each red point is $1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 = 15$, the degree of beauty of each orange point is $2 + 3 + 4 + 5 = 14$, the degree of beauty of each green point is $4 + 5 = 9$, the degree of beauty of each blue point is $5$ and the degree of beauty of each gray point is $0$. Therefore, $*f*(5) = 5·15 + 4·14 + 4·9 + 8·5 = 207$.

Similarly, $*f*(1) = 5, *f*(2) = 23, *f*(3) = 50, *f*(4) = 102$ and consequently ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/57bd086c10ae597f8cbd2785a92ae473165e1141.png).
statementZhMd:
*一切红色的东西都会吓到年兽。红纸也是如此，还有你——在 Codeforces 上，无论是潜在的还是已经变红的。*

大班班有一张铺满无限晶格点的纸，这些晶格点组成面积相等的正方形。他最喜欢的闭合图形是圆，因为它既美观又简单。得到这张纸后，他准备对其进行剪纸。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/82edc897487bb94b56952d372bcbcb46bd964bb6.png)

他在纸上画了 $*n*$ 个同心圆，并将这些圆编号为 $1$ 到 $*n*$，使得每个圆的圆心都是同一个晶格点，且第 $*k*$ 个圆的半径为 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/bd3647accc3b41427aa4218c550a610cef4bfdeb.png) 倍晶格边的长度。

定义一个晶格点的美丽度为包含该点（包括点位于圆周上的情况）的所有圆的**编号**之和。班班原本想询问所有晶格点的美丽度总和，但后来改变了主意。

将一张画有 $*n*$ 个圆的纸上所有晶格点的美丽度总和定义为 $*f*(*n*)$，请你求出 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/1c6463774e657bd7c8665c65ff8deb39afdcf644.png)。

## 输入格式

第一行包含一个整数 $*m*$ $(1 ≤ *m* ≤ 10^{12})$。

## 输出格式

第一行输出一个整数，表示 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/1c6463774e657bd7c8665c65ff8deb39afdcf644.png)。

## 说明

下图展示了一张画有 $5$ 个圆的纸。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/b63097ed9dc567853f8c13b2a90317a6ad36bb91.png)

其中共有 $5$ 类晶格点：每个红色点的美丽度为 $1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 = 15$，每个橙色点的美丽度为 $2 + 3 + 4 + 5 = 14$，每个绿色点的美丽度为 $4 + 5 = 9$，每个蓝色点的美丽度为 $5$，每个灰色点的美丽度为 $0$。因此，$*f*(5) = 5·15 + 4·14 + 4·9 + 8·5 = 207$。

类似地，$*f*(1) = 5$、$*f*(2) = 23$、$*f*(3) = 50$、$*f*(4) = 102$，因此 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/57bd086c10ae597f8cbd2785a92ae473165e1141.png)。
